text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
-- Industry minister Franck Borotra calls for the building of a major defence electronics hub bringing together all players in the sector, with Thomson-CSF acting as a central element.
-- ITT sold 3 million Alcatel Alsthom shares to a U.S. investment fund.
-- Paris bourse CAC 40 blue-chip index sets record high.
-- OECD report cheers Prime Minister Alain Juppe's policy.
-- Government may announce terms of Thomson privatisation on Feb 26.
-- Some German defence industrialists worried by a possible 100-percent-French solution for Thomson-CSF.
-- OECD sees 2.5 percent growth rate for France in 1997.
-- Railroad line from Paris to Toulouse may be the first to rely on oscillating train technology.

-- PSA Peugeot Citroen chairman Jacques Calvet, expected to retire from carmaker in September, considers returning to banking. According to newspaper, he has offered to take over top job at Credit Lyonnais.
-- OECD report calls for adjustments to French minimum wage (SMIC), to adapt to worker's age and geographical area. It also calls for increased flexibility in hiring and laying off.
-- OECD foresees 2.5 percent French growth for 1997, raising expectations the government will succeed in meeting criteria for single European currency.
